name: Antigua
title: Holidays in Antigua
intro: A beach for every day of the year, calm turquoise bays and Sunday sunsets at Shirley Heights. Here's what Antigua is like, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Antigua drives on the left, like the UK, and US dollars are widely taken. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to April is dry and sunny, with Christmas and Easter the busiest and dearest. Summer is hot with lower prices. Hurricane season runs June to November, peaking in September and October.

things.name: Beaches
things.blurb: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches. Darkwood, Jolly Beach and Half Moon Bay are good for families.

things.name: Stingray City
things.blurb: Stand in shallow water and feed friendly southern stingrays.

things.name: Nelson's Dockyard
things.blurb: A restored Georgian naval dockyard with a museum, cafés and yachts.

things.name: Shirley Heights Lookout
things.blurb: Sunday evening steel bands and barbecue with a famous sunset view over English Harbour.

things.name: Rainforest zip line
things.blurb: Zip lines and rope bridges through the treetops, for children aged about eight and up.

things.name: Catamaran trip
things.blurb: A day's sail with snorkelling stops, sometimes round the island or across to Barbuda.

faqs.question: Is Antigua good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's English-speaking, with calm beaches, all-inclusive resorts and a direct flight from the UK of about eight and a half hours.

faqs.question: Is Christmas a good time to go?
faqs.answer: Yes, the weather is dry and warm. It's the dearest time of year, so book early.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit without a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Ten to fourteen nights, to make the long flight worthwhile.
